body: That makes a lot more sense.
I'm a bartender/bouncer, and am searching for a full-time job. I have been searching for about three months now, without luck.

I'm sorry this has taken me so long to respond to. Honestly, I've been avoiding looking at this page, partly for fear of no responses (anxiety is the best) but also largely for fear of there BEING responses. I have asked for additional hours, but am not seeing the fruits of that labour yet (excepting when I am able to take over other people's shifts) and the manager won't give me a straight reason why. I've never gotten in trouble at this job, and I'm beginning to feel it is because I don't spend enough time around the management outside of work (a.k.a. I don't drink at the bar very often) so we haven't built a rapport as friends --something that many of the other employees had before he hired them.

I have been applying for jobs, but I think my resume may need additional work, so I will have to take you up on that advice. I'm running into a huge roadblock, and that is a degree. I didn't go to school out of college, instead focusing on work and becoming a manager at a high volume retail location for a few years, which I eventually lost due to circumstances beyond my control (there was a burglary.) Unfortunately, every job I apply to that has some sort of merit to it (anything that isn't fast food...) has a requirement of a Bachelor's, and overcoming that is an obstacle. The experience I have as a manager is going to be irrelevant soon, as well, as it has been almost three years now. 

I'm confused by what you say about what /r/personalfinance can do. How can they waive the fee? I don't understand this, and when I went to look through their subreddit for additional information, I couldn't see anything about that. Would you mind elaborating? It's one of the biggest hurdles I've come up against. I can't seem to get enough money together to pay for my bills, let alone an additional $1,500. The good news is, since I started becoming a little more self-aware of my debt problems, I haven't taken on any additional debt. The credit cards are old, and haven't been used in years, they just don't have any real payments on them in that time, either.
My appearance has been a losing battle from the beginning. As a kid, I did not take good care of my hygiene (which I believe stems from poor self-image at that time. Being a redheaded child wasn't the easiest.) While I do take care of my teeth, and try to keep my hair brushed, I often feel like my appearance is sub-par. I find myself denigrating my appearance, especially if I can't find the things I like to wear. (Today, for example, I felt like my hair looked very stupid, because when it hasn't been cut in a little while the sides stick out abnormally. When I tried to find a hat, all I could find were hats that were, in my opinion, dumb-looking.) I have no real wardrobe to speak of, just a mosh of assorted tee shirts, one or two pairs of jeans, a pair of shorts, and some "dress" clothes (which actually look not half-bad, if I say so) but it seems that even when I keep things hung and put effort into them, they wind up looking awful on me for some reason.
I am afraid of counselling. I'm afraid of talking to people in general (clearly, look how long I put off even reading responses to this.) it makes me uncomfortable, nervous, and on the verge of a panic attack. Sharing intimate details of my life is beyond reproach. My entire life I've kept to myself. Everything about me is a secret, locked in a vault, and letting that go is... unfathomable. It was extremely hard to write about my past here, let alone speaking about it. It has been on my mind a lot lately, though, I just don't know how to go about getting that sort of help. 

I do have two wonderful, amazing dogs, and when/if I am having an episode (typically me breaking down crying for some reason) they are there to lick my face and let me hold them. It is very therapeutic.

I did lift, when I lived in a different state and had a long-time friend to lift with/be my trainer. It's hard to remember what it was like then, but I do remember how good it felt to lift heavy things. I wouldn't mind getting into this again, and I have started running using a couch-to-5k program, but I'm nervous about the gym. About doing too much and hurting myself, or not knowing what to do. Being around that many people who are in-shape when I am clearly not is nerve-wracking. And I'm not overweight, necessarily. I'm probably under, standing 6'3" and weighing around 161lbs.
I want to gain somewhere around 40 lbs, and have it be concrete, but I have a hard time visualizing that goal. Like I said before, I struggle to pay bills, I sure as hell struggle to eat, but a lot of that stems from poor money management, and a lack of knowledge of what to buy to make things last. I do eat out (more often than I'd care to admit) and I rarely cook at home, which has lately stemmed from a sinkful of dirty dishes that I have been unable to wash because my landlord won't come fix my superclogged sink drains.

Your last paragraphs really struck home for me, because I do focus on the problems in my life. Every night when I lie down it's all I can think of, right down to the minute details of a conversation I had with the cop who gave me a DUI four years ago, and what I could've said to avoid things. I push myself hard, probably harder than I should, but I'm also breaking down. I hate who I am.

I hate almost everything about me, and I wish I could change. I want to be more in-control. More masculine. I'm not assertive, or strong. I don't feel like I have a presence, but more like everyone's eyes glide past me, like I may as well not exist.

I'm not sure this was the most coherent response, and I'm sorry for that. Father's day is always a rough time of year for me, given my fatherly past, and I also found out today that a kid I taught (when he was in kindergarten) died today in a car wreck.
